newsitem.title: INDIA: IMF chief urges India to phase out oil subsidy.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief urges India to phase out oil subsidy.

text.p: International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus on Wednesday urged India to phase out state subsidies on petroleum products and move towards a system of market-determined prices.

"It would be important to correct large...subsidies," Camdessus told a news conference in the Indian capital. "The large subsidy on petroleum products should also be phased out through moving towards a system of market-determined prices."
The Indian government owes domestic oil companies, which sell petroleum products on the domestic market at prices well below international levels, an estimated 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion).
The 15-party coalition government has been debating whether to raise domestic prices for the second time since it took power last June.
The Petroleum Ministry has pressed to have the subsidy programme overhauled so that Indian domestic prices are more closely aligned with world prices. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
